answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through xylem acoustic attestation. Each agent couples a sensor to a living vine to record cavitation events. When sap tension breaks water columns inside hollow vascular conduits, the snap emits an unpredictable acoustic pulse. Creating fake identities forces an attacker to maintain scarce physical plants and dedicated acoustic probes per node. However, high soil moisture suppresses cavitation, causing false rejections.
